newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BAUMA SEES IPO FULLY SUBSCRIBED.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BAUMA SEES IPO FULLY SUBSCRIBED.

text.p: The 1.2-million-share initital public offering by Polish paving-stone maker Bauma SA will likely be fully subscribed without its underwriters needing to take up shares, the firm's president said on Friday.

"The queues at points carrying out our subscription give the hope that the help of the underwriters won't be necessary," Andrzej Kozlowski told a news conference about the issue at 10 zlotys per share that ends on Friday.
Six companies are underwriting the issue, whose result is due on January 29.

Polish Private Equity 1 and Polish Private Equity 2 are underwriting 300,000 shares each, Investment house BWE SA and Bank Wschodnio-Europejski SA 200,000 shares each and the brokerages of bank BRE and Bank Ochrony Srodowiska SA 100,000 shares each.
Before the issue Bauma, which seeks a parallel floor listing, had 130,421 shares, all approved for public trade.

The company made a net profit of 418,000 zlotys on 15.4 million zlotys in sales in 1995. It expects to net 1.5 million zlotys in 1996 and 2.1 million in 1997 on 14 million zlotys and 19.6 million zlotys in sales respectively.
